_notice: Default values for Multi-D sharing factors. Entries flagged provisional:true are estimates — refine with Eurostat, World Bank, FAOSTAT and Danish EPA (Miljøstyrelsen) before publication. Entries flagged provisional:false name a dataset and a vintage in their own source field. AR was moved onto Global Carbon Budget 2024 (territorial fossil + cement, 1850-2020, fossil-only on both sides) and is no longer an estimate; its previous 2-significant-figure values mixed a fossil-only numerator with a net-CO2 denominator, which is why values here are stored to full precision.

AR.description: Acquired rights — historical cumulative CO2 emissions share
AR.unit: t CO2 cumulative 1850-2020, territorial fossil fuel + cement, land-use change EXCLUDED on both sides
AR.source: Global Carbon Budget 2024 (Friedlingstein et al. 2024, doi:10.5194/essd-17-965-2025), file National_Carbon_Emissions_2024v1.01.xlsx, sheet 'Territorial Emissions': sum of annual values 1850-2020 x 3.664 MtCO2/MtC. Denmark 1114.0005 MtC = 4081.6977 MtCO2; World 462120.6397 MtC = 1693210.0239 MtCO2 (the World column includes bunker fuels). SCOPE: fossil + cement on BOTH sides. The AR principle allocates ozone depletion, particulate matter and photochemical ozone formation - all combustion- and industry-driven, none produced by land conversion - so land-use change is a different physical process here, not a missing term; climate change is allocated by EpC in this preset, which is where a net-CO2 basis would belong. WINDOW: 1850-2020 is the window this principle declares, and is deliberately NOT extended to GCB's 2023 coverage, which would mix a grandfathering window with the carbon budget's own 2025 baseline for no methodological gain. Both values are stored to 9 significant figures: the previous 2-s.f. rounding is part of why a scope mismatch went unnoticed.

layer2.source: Passenger cars ~60% of Danish transport GHG × transport ~25% of national total ≈ 0.15. Provisional — refine with Danish EPA sectoral breakdown.
